```{r}
#| label: obx-setup
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONSOLE FACSIMILES -- render scaffolding, hidden (include: false). Same
# mechanism as anova.qmd: pane_facsimile.R defines the capture-once /
# display-twice helpers in their own dot-named environment (.obx). Each block
# below is one call whose code STRING is both printed into the page and
# executed once, so the shown code and the run code cannot drift. An
# unexpected error in any block HALTS the render (the publish gate).
#
# Devices, by the OUTPUT-REGISTER rule: the prose READS the output of blocks 1
# and 3, so those panes render OPEN (.obx$show_console(fence = TRUE)). Block
# 2's result is a chart, not Console output: its code is a plain fence and the
# chart is drawn by a chunk that runs the same code string (anova.qmd's
# block 8).
#
# PUBLICATION TABLES, PAGE 3 (S422). It uses page 1's saved results and page
# 2's tables, t1 and t2; block 1 makes them again, without files (print =
# FALSE), so the page and its script also work in a fresh session.
#
# jstats is NOT pre-loaded: block 1 teaches library(jstats), and R prints the
# startup message on first attach only. joutput()/joptions() are left alone.
# The page WRITES one Word file into the working directory; the clean-slate
# line below removes it before the blocks run, and the teardown after.
#
# HOW-TO LAYOUT (S344). No top boxes: the shared material lives once on
# howtos.qmd, and this page points there.
#
# S428 (the S427 wording pass, Fable 5.2, okayed by Jeff): the recurring
# changes A-M and the page's 19 numbered changes; the reading box's "its
# second line says so" gated on the wide table's second line.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

options(width = 80)   # match a default 80-column console for table alignment
options(jstats.attach.noninteractive = TRUE)   # let block 1 show the real startup message

.sv_files <- c("Report.docx")
.sv_clean <- function() {
  f <- .sv_files[file.exists(.sv_files)]
  if (length(f)) file.remove(f)
  invisible(NULL)
}
.sv_clean()

source("pane_facsimile.R")   # defines .obx (dot-named); turns the output color on
```

## Several tables and a chart in one file

**Publication tables &middot; Page 3**\
*It uses the results saved on
[1. Saving results](tables-saving-results.qmd) and the tables made on
[2. Making a table in Word](tables-in-word.qmd).*

A report or an article usually has several tables, and a chart or two. This page
is a hands-on run-through of putting them in one Word file, numbered in order,
with one call to `jtable()`.

This page follows the pattern of every How-To: numbered blocks of code that
build one script, with the finished script to download at the bottom.
[Using the How-To pages](howtos.qmd#using-the-how-to-pages) explains the
pattern, and how to reset your session if something goes wrong.

Block 1 repeats the steps from pages 1 and 2 that saved the two results and made
their tables, `t1` and `t2`, so this page works in a fresh session too. If all
four are still listed in your **Environment** pane, running block 1 does no
harm: it makes them again.

### 1. Load jstats, and make the results and their tables again

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 1. Load jstats, and make the results and their tables again ------

## Load jstats and community, make community the default data frame, save
## page 1's two results again, and make their tables, t1 and t2.
## quiet = TRUE skips jload()'s report, which page 1 shows; overwrite = TRUE
## replaces a copy loaded earlier without asking first. print = FALSE keeps
## each command's output out of the Console; with no file =, jtable()
## writes nothing to Word yet
library(jstats)
jload("community", overwrite = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
juse(community)
d1 <- jdesc(Age, Income, WellbeingScore, print = FALSE)
m1 <- jlm(WellbeingScore ~ Age + Income, print = FALSE)
t1 <- jtable(d1, print = FALSE)
t2 <- jtable(m1, print = FALSE))---", fence = TRUE,
  lead = "The command lines are shown; the standalone <code>##</code> comment lines aren't -- running a comment just echoes it back and does nothing.")
```

jstats and `community` are loaded, and the two results and their tables are
saved, with no output in the Console. On page 2 each table went to a Word file
of its own; here the tables stay in R until block 3 writes them to one file.

### 2. A chart

A chart from `jplot()` can be saved with `<-`, just as a result can. Here the
chart is a bar chart of the region each respondent lives in, saved as `p1`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.b2 <- r"---(## ---- 2. A chart -------------------------------------------------------

## A bar chart of Region, saved as p1. It appears in the Plots tab
## (lower-right pane)
p1 <- jplot(Region))---"
.fence <- strrep("`", 3)
cat(.fence, "r\n", .b2, "\n", .fence, "\n", sep = "")
```

The chart appears in the **Plots** tab of the lower-right pane. (`jplot()` also
shows the chart's title and its number of cases, 103, in the Console.)

```{r}
#| label: tables-several-chart
#| echo: false
#| results: hide
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-alt: "A bar chart of the number of respondents in each region of residence, one gray bar per region, the count printed above each: North 27, South 20, East 31, West 25."
eval(parse(text = .b2))
```

### 3. Tables and a chart in one file

Put the tables and the chart together with base R's `list()`, and `jtable()`
writes them all to one Word file, in the order of the list.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 3. Tables and a chart in one file --------------------------------

## list() is base R: it puts the two tables and the chart together, in
## this order, and jtable() writes them all to one Word file
jtable(list(t1, p1, t2), file = "Report.docx", open = TRUE))---", fence = TRUE)
```

The Console lists what went into the file, in order, and ends with where the
file was written. The tables are numbered in the order given, so the regression
table, which was Table 1 in its own file on page 2, is Table 2 here. The chart
is Figure 1: figures are numbered separately from tables. The chart gets a
caption in the same form as a table's: the number, then the title and N.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reading this output"}
- **Each table and figure** gets two lines: its number and title, then what it
  holds and the kind of page it goes on (portrait here). The pairs of lines
  come in the order of the list, which is the order the tables and figures
  have in the Word file.
- **The last line** counts what went into the file, and says where the file was
  written.
- **A wide table**, such as a crosstab across several groups, goes on a
  landscape page of its own, and its second line says so; the pages around it
  stay portrait.
:::

To add another table later, save its result, make its table, and add the table
to the list, in the place it should have in the file. Close `Report.docx` in
Word, then run the line again: `jtable()` asks before replacing the file, and
you answer `y`.

Each table here holds one result. Page 4,
[Several results in one table](tables-several-results.qmd), puts two
regression models side by side in a single table.

```{r}
#| label: prose-gates
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROSE GATES -- hidden. Each stopifnot() below is one statement the prose
# makes about what the package does; a false one HALTS the render, the same
# publish gate the blocks have.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.msgs <- function(expr) {         # what a call prints, both streams, as one string
  m <- character(0)
  o <- withCallingHandlers(utils::capture.output(expr),
                           message = function(c) { m <<- c(m, conditionMessage(c))
                                                   invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  paste(c(o, m), collapse = "\n")
}
.td <- tempfile("sv-"); dir.create(.td)
# block 1: nothing printed
.m1q <- .msgs({ jdesc(Age, Income, WellbeingScore, print = FALSE)
                jlm(WellbeingScore ~ Age + Income, print = FALSE)
                jtable(d1, print = FALSE); jtable(m1, print = FALSE) })
# block 2: jplot() prints its title and N; the alt text's counts
grDevices::pdf(NULL)
.m2 <- .msgs(jplot(Region))
invisible(grDevices::dev.off())
.reg <- table(haven::as_factor(community$Region))
# block 3: the order and the numbering
.m3 <- .msgs(jtable(list(t1, p1, t2), file = file.path(.td, "R.docx")))
.pos <- function(s) regexpr(s, .m3, fixed = TRUE)
# the reading box: a wide table goes landscape, and its second line says so
.x1 <- jcrosstab(Volunteer ~ Region, print = FALSE)
.m_wide <- .msgs(jtable(.x1))
.mw <- strsplit(.m_wide, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
.mw_t <- grep("^Table 1\\. ", .mw)
.m_mix <- .msgs(jtable(list(t1, jtable(.x1, print = FALSE)), file = file.path(.td, "M.docx")))

stopifnot(
  !nzchar(.m1q),
  grepl("Bar Chart: Region", .m2, fixed = TRUE), grepl("Analysis N: 103", .m2, fixed = TRUE),
  identical(names(.reg), c("North", "South", "East", "West")),
  identical(as.integer(.reg), c(27L, 20L, 31L, 25L)),
  file.exists("Report.docx"),
  .pos("Table 1. Descriptive") > 0, .pos("Figure 1. Region") > .pos("Table 1. Descriptive"),
  .pos("Table 2. Regression") > .pos("Figure 1. Region"),
  grepl("2 tables and 1 figure written to", .m3, fixed = TRUE),
  grepl("on a landscape page", .m_wide, fixed = TRUE),
  length(.mw_t) == 1L, grepl("on a landscape page", .mw[.mw_t + 1L], fixed = TRUE),
  grepl("3 variables, on a portrait page.", .m_mix, fixed = TRUE),
  grepl("on a landscape page", .m_mix, fixed = TRUE)
)
unlink(.td, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Take the whole script with you

That's the full run-through. If you'd like the entire script in one file to
keep and reuse, download it here. Put your own tables and charts in the list,
in the order you want them in the file.

The file is the finished version of the script you built: the same code, in the
same order. If you run the file a second time, `jtable()` asks before replacing
`Report.docx`; the file's first lines say what to answer.
[Using the How-To pages](howtos.qmd#using-the-how-to-pages) says more about
finished scripts and how to run one.
